Title: Staged roadmap
Body:
The staged roadmap

Learn the skill, build the artifact, demonstrate its exit gate, then integrate. There are 12 required preparation projects before lem-in and two optional preparation projects after it. The order follows actual dependencies; the visualizer never blocks core completion.

Planning, not a deadline: required prep is 142 focused hours; core integration is 40, totaling 182 before review. Allow another 25–50% for reading, debugging and review: about 228–273 hours. At 20 focused hours per week, plan roughly 12–14 weeks. The complete optional visualizer adds 42 base hours, or about 53–63 with review. Learner completion is unassessed.

STAGE 01 · 32 HOURS

Go and colony data

  1. P01 · Go Field Notebook — 8h. Learn types, modules, returned errors and tests.
  2. P02 · Bounded File Reader — 10h. Handle files, EOF, line endings and read limits.
  3. P03 · Colony Grammar State Machine — 14h. Validate the actual language and preserve accepted echo.

Readiness gate: demonstrate the grammar mutation table, bounded-reader fault tests and no accepted partial model. A valid parse need not have a route yet.

STAGE 02 · 30 HOURS

Graphs and turn safety

  1. P04 · Undirected Graph Inventory — 8h. Stable identity, adjacency, components and ordinary cycles.
  2. P05 · Queue and BFS Route Finder — 10h. Distance, parents and unreachable targets.
  3. P06 · Turn Safety Simulator — 12h. Independent atomic validation of concurrent movement.

Readiness gate: a pipeline into a vacated room passes; stationary-room collisions and shared-tunnel swaps fail. Prove BFS distance for one ant and explain why it is insufficient for all ants.

STAGE 03 · 56 HOURS

Exact optimization

  1. P07 · Traffic and Ant Allocation Lab — 8h. Throughput, makespan and a greedy counterexample.
  2. P08 · Residual Flow Workbench — 14h. Reverse arcs, conservation, integrality and cuts.
  3. P09 · Capacity Through Time — 16h. Room splits, waiting and shared tunnel-time bottlenecks.
  4. P10 · Exact Deadline Planner — 18h. Deadline search, extraction, ant IDs and proof.

Readiness gate: show both directions of the schedule/flow correspondence and feasibility at T plus a lower-bound witness at T-1. Resource refusal must never become false in a deadline probe.

STAGE 04 · 24 HOURS

Verification and release

  1. P11 · Adversarial Validator and Tiny Oracle — 14h. Transcript checks, occupancy-state search and differential evidence.
  2. P12 · Deterministic and Bounded Release Lab — 10h. Checked budgets, stable streams and reproducibility.

Readiness gate: complete the 3294-case small-graph campaign, report every budget skip and catch targeted transcript mutations. Compilation of a TODO starter does not satisfy this gate.

INTEGRATION · 40 HOURS

Build lem-in

L01 · Full lem-in guide →

Bring the prepared components into one CLI. Review the assignment brief, academy policies and requirement coverage. Produce a minimum-turn schedule, independent replay evidence, an exactness argument and measured source-audit compatibility results.

Readiness gate: all required behavior, enabled solution tests, exactness proof, tiny evidence and process/resource contract pass instructor review. The hub does not set completion automatically.

OPTIONAL STAGE 05 · 22 HOURS

Prepare the visualizer

  1. P13 · Replay Stream Decoder — 10h. Validated streams and immutable snapshots.
  2. P14 · Go Raster and GIF Studio — 12h. Coordinates, pixels, palettes and GIF timing.

Readiness gate: decoder rejects corrupt/truncated streams; rendered GIF decodes back with correct frames, delays and independent pixel storage.

OPTIONAL INTEGRATION · 20 HOURS

Build the Go GIF visualizer

V01 · Optional visualizer guide →

Consume solver stdout and generate farm.gif plus legend/replay text using only standard Go packages. Validate the real pipeline, safe output handling and viewed motion. A 3D display is outside this academy bonus's required scope.

Team and scheduling guidance

Estimates assume an individual with basic programming experience, regular review and no prior Go/graph/flow knowledge. Pairing can help discussion but does not halve concept time. Add time for a learner who needs the prerequisite bridge; allow strong learners to challenge a preparation gate with an equivalent working artifact and explanation. Team size is a local teaching decision, not an upstream requirement.

Title: Prerequisites and workspace
Body:
Start here: prerequisites and workspace

Bring basic programming experience, including variables, functions, conditions and loops, plus files, terminal use and Git. JavaScript and HTML familiarity are useful background, but no Go, graph algorithms, flow theory or scheduling knowledge is assumed.

Before P01

  1. Be able to create a folder, edit a text file, run a terminal command and describe its exit status.
  2. Use Git to commit a small change and inspect a diff. Keep exercises in separate directories.
  3. Explain a loop and a function returning a value in any familiar language. If those are unfamiliar, take a basic programming bridge before this track; its duration is not included in the estimates.

Required tools

Install a supported Go toolchain that understands Go 1.22 or newer, on a 64-bit target. The supplied modules declare Go 1.22 to use a conservative API baseline; the hub's local validation records the actual installed version. Use a text editor, terminal and ZIP extractor. No external Go modules are required.

go version
go env GOOS GOARCH
go test ./...
go vet ./...

Run each starter's commands inside its extracted directory containing go.mod. The academy root is a different module for publication tooling. Keep student changes outside the generated public/downloads folder so rebuilds cannot overwrite them.

Learning map

P01 teaches Go foundations. P02/P03 teach file and grammar boundaries. P04/P05 teach graphs and BFS. P06 teaches turn invariants. P07 introduces traffic and allocation. P08/P09/P10 teach every new optimization concept before integration. P11/P12 teach adversarial evidence and bounded release. P13/P14 introduce bonus-only stream and raster skills after the core build.

Commands across platforms

Go commands are the same across platforms. A built executable uses ./lem-in on Unix and .\lem-in.exe in PowerShell. Avoid assuming shell redirection/pipelines preserve UTF-8 bytes identically across PowerShell versions; use the Go os/exec harness for byte-exact pipeline tests. The final CLI still requires the file argument upstream requests.

How to use a guide

Read mandatory sections first, trace the self-checks by hand, download the unfinished starter, implement one component and enable its acceptance tests. Add failure tests, run the verification cases and answer the engineering prompts aloud with a reviewer. Completing a reading page does not establish project readiness.

Continue to the staged roadmap →

Title: Exact academy contract
Body:
Exact academy contract

U identifies upstream requirements; A identifies academy decisions resolving unspecified details. Review these policies with the institution before using this curriculum for a formal external audit. These decisions are part of the academy exercises and independently testable.

U · Required behavior

Use Go and only standard packages. Read the colony from one file argument, send n ants from start to end in the fewest movement turns, respect ordinary room capacity one and undirected tunnel capacity one per turn, and print accepted input followed by L-number/destination movement tokens. Names need not be numbers; coordinates are ints. Ignore unknown commands. Malformed data and no-route inputs require the invalid-data error prefix.

A · Input transport and echo

  • Read at most 1 MiB and 4096 bytes per physical line, excluding its line terminator. Accept LF/CRLF; reject bare CR and NUL. A final newline is optional.
  • Normalize CRLF to LF and append one final LF if missing. Preserve other accepted line bytes, including comments, unknown commands and surrounding whitespace. A valid colony has no blank data lines, so exactly one blank line separates echo from moves.
  • Classification uses trimmed line text; room fields use whitespace separation. The normalized original text, not regenerated structs, supplies the success echo.

A · Grammar and terminal state machine

  • Phases are count, rooms, links. Comments begin with # after surrounding whitespace is trimmed. Exact ##start/##end are known commands; any other ## line is ignored semantically. Other # lines are comments. Unknown commands may occur in any phase.
  • Count is decimal [1-9][0-9]* in 1..10000. Leading zeros, signs, fractions and overflow are invalid. Known terminal commands before count are invalid.
  • A room is exactly name x y. Its nonempty valid UTF-8 name has no Unicode whitespace or controls and does not start with L or #. Hyphens are allowed. Names compare bytewise and are case-sensitive.
  • Coordinates match optional + or - followed by one or more decimal digits and fit a signed 64-bit int. A 64-bit Go target is required. Duplicate coordinates are valid; room names cannot repeat.
  • Each terminal marker occurs once and binds to the next room, skipping comments/unknown commands. A second marker while pending, a repeat marker, a marker in link phase or pending marker at EOF is invalid. Start/end must be distinct.
  • A tunnel has no whitespace. Consider every hyphen split whose two substrings name existing rooms: exactly one split must match. Zero matches or multiple matches fail. This preserves hyphenated names without inventing a new delimiter. Reject self-links and canonical duplicate pairs, including reversed duplicates.
  • Once a link is accepted, room definitions are closed. A room after links is invalid. Missing required structure, bad field counts and unknown noncommand lines fail.

U + A · Cycles, disconnectedness and turns

Self-links are invalid, consistent with the source's error examples and badexample01. Ordinary cycles among distinct rooms are valid and search must terminate. Disconnected extra rooms are valid when a start-end route exists; an unreachable end is an invalid-data/no-route result.

Upstream usage shows a pipeline into rooms vacated that turn. The academy therefore validates turns as batches: derive sources from old state, account for all departures, then arrivals, checking ordinary occupancy at the next boundary. Token order does not change legality. One undirected tunnel use total still forbids opposite swaps. Cyclic rotations of three or more ants are batch-valid under this convention; they are unnecessary for optimum completion and no part of the planner relies on retaining them. End is absorbing in accepted academy schedules. Keeping an arrived ant at end is without loss because it frees nonterminal resources.

A · Exact planning and deterministic output

The taught method searches the first feasible deadline in [d,d+n-1], where d is BFS distance. Feasibility uses integral flow on a time-expanded graph with split room capacity, holdovers and shared tunnel-time gadgets. Same-side gadget traversals become waits. P09/P10 contain the correspondence and minimum-deadline proofs.

Canonicalize names and edges bytewise, insert model arcs in a documented stable order, extract unit trajectories in that order and assign ant IDs 1..n. Ant ID spelling is decimal [1-9][0-9]* without signs or leading zeros. Output only moved ants, ID-ascending within each turn, separated by one space. No trailing spaces, empty movement turns or extra diagnostics; every line ends LF. Independent correct solvers may select different optimum schedules. Repeated runs of one implementation must match bytes.

A · Process outcomes

Result streams and exit codes
OutcomestdoutstderrExit
SuccessFull echo + blank separator + movesEmpty by default0
Malformed / no routeERROR: invalid data format, optional suffix, LF; no echoEmpty by default1
Usage / file / writer I/OEmpty before output; may be partial after writer failureUseful usage or I/O error2
Resource refusal / timeoutEmpty; no claimed planERROR: resource limit exceeded, optional detail3

The upstream audit displays invalid-data messages on stdout but does not fully specify all streams/exits. The academy chooses these explicit outcomes. A write failure must never append an invalid-data line to a partial success transcript.

A · Resource envelope and honest limits

Default maxima are 10000 ants, 10000 rooms, 50000 tunnels, 200000 expanded vertices, 1000000 stored residual arcs, 4000000 stored ant-time position cells, 16 MiB formatted output and 240 seconds total planning time, in addition to input limits. Preflight checked count arithmetic and monitor work. Valid input may exceed the computation budget; report resource refusal separately, without claiming infeasibility or returning a heuristic labelled optimal. Successful runs remain exact.

Model upper counts at horizon T are 2(T+1)V+2TE vertices and (2T+1)V+5TE original arcs; residual storage doubles original arcs. Counts alone are not a total byte guarantee: adjacency headers, metadata, extraction and output also consume memory. Profile the actual implementation and document the measured envelope.

A · Bonus

The optional renderer writes a 2D animated GIF using standard Go image packages, with text legend and replay. Default dimensions are 320×240, four subframes per turn, 40-centisecond initial/final holds and turn duration. Maximum dimensions are 1280×720, frames 2000 and total stored pixels 50000000. Budget breaches fail explicitly; they do not silently omit turns. There is no required JavaScript, GUI library, external font package or 3D implementation.

Title: Lem-in assignment brief
Body:
Lem-in assignment brief

Build a Go CLI named lem-in that reads an ant colony from a file argument and brings every numbered ant from start to end in the fewest turns. Preserve the original assignment separately from the academy's explicit implementation policies.

Open the full guided assignment → Read the original upstream brief

Inputs and outputs

A colony contains a positive ant count, room records name x y, terminal directives ##start/##end and undirected name-name tunnel records. Room names are not assumed numeric or ordered. On success, print the accepted colony, one blank separator and one movement line per turn using L<number>-<destination> tokens. Display only ants that move.

Constraints that determine the algorithm

All ants start together. Ordinary rooms hold one ant; terminal rooms can hold many. Every tunnel is a shared undirected resource usable once per turn, and every ant can move through only one tunnel per turn. A shortest path for one ant can be a poor multi-ant choice. An exact solution must optimize final arrival time while avoiding both room collisions and tunnel reuse.

Errors and edge cases

Handle malformed counts/records, missing or repeated terminals, duplicate rooms/tunnels, unknown endpoints, invalid integers, self-links and no route deliberately with the required invalid-data prefix. Ordinary graph cycles and irrelevant disconnected rooms require safe traversal. Ignore unknown commands. The academy contract resolves whitespace, echo, integer spelling, hyphen ambiguity, turn ordering, streams/exits and resource boundaries.

Submission

  • Go source using only standard packages, build/run instructions and meaningful tests.
  • A correctness argument for the exact planning method, including capacities, waits, ant extraction and minimum deadline.
  • An independent transcript/movement validator and tiny-instance optimality evidence.
  • Adversarial fixtures, deterministic output checks, complexity/resource notes and measured audit example results.

Optional continuation

After core readiness, complete P13/P14 and the Go GIF visualizer bonus. Coordinates become display data there. The bonus does not replace the required CLI or optimality proof.

Title: Optional visualizer brief
Body:
Optional Go visualizer brief

Build a standard-library Go program that consumes a complete lem-in transcript on stdin and writes an animated ant-farm GIF, room legend and text replay. Validate the stream independently before rendering it.

./lem-in ant-farm.txt | ./visualizer

Default outputs are farm.gif, legend.txt and replay.txt. The GIF shows rooms/tunnels from coordinates and moves ants along their actual tunnels, retaining waits and terminal arrivals. Negative, coincident and zero-span coordinates must be handled safely. Text output preserves arbitrary valid names and every ant's identity.

Preparation is P13 · Replay Stream Decoder, then P14 · Go Raster and GIF Studio. Integration is V01 · Optional Ant-Farm GIF Visualizer.

Why GIF

Go's standard library includes raster images and GIF encoding, making an animated file feasible without browser programming or third-party graphics. A viewer displays the output; viewer playback timing can vary. The academy requires decode-back metadata tests plus viewed motion. 3D appears as an audit extra, outside this bonus's required 2D scope.

Readiness gate

Core L01 reviewed first; valid/invalid pipeline tests; immutable replay; safe coordinate transform; frame/pixel budgets; output collision/cleanup tests; no trails; correct final state; accurate legend/replay. A legal but slow transcript may be rendered, but the visualizer must not describe it as optimal.

Title: Instructor readiness and review
Body:
Instructor readiness and review

This curriculum is complete as an instructional artifact, with unfinished student implementations. No learner is assessed or marked complete by the hub. Instructors must pilot the work and review solutions before using the track as formal assessment.

Instructor prerequisite gate

  1. Build and test a small Go CLI and explain Reader/Writer ownership, error wrapping and slice aliasing.
  2. Trace BFS, residual cancellation and a minimum-cut witness without relying on a library solver.
  3. Explain both directions of the time-expanded reduction, including room splitting, shared undirected edge gadgets and same-side waiting normalization.
  4. Explain [d,d+n-1], monotone deadline search, integral extraction and why a budget refusal is not infeasibility.
  5. Run the independent occupancy-state oracle and understand its tiny scope and exponential growth.

Before the cohort

Review the source adaptation notes and agree the academy grammar/turn/error policies with local auditors. Check supported Go installation, 64-bit targets, ZIP extraction and all local reading links. Run the publication build and scaffold checks. Pilot the first three projects with a beginner and the exact-planning block with a second reviewer; estimates are planning allowances, not measured cohort medians.

Project review procedure

  1. Ask the learner to show the artifact and one concrete user-facing behavior before discussing implementation.
  2. Walk every component's self-check and verification exit gate. Ask for expected versus actual bytes on a failure case.
  3. Inspect tests with all relevant acceptance skips removed. A green starter compile is insufficient.
  4. Introduce one targeted mutation, such as missing reverse capacity or duplicated tunnel use, and require an existing test to detect it.
  5. Discuss at least two engineering prompts and one practical task. Record feedback in the institution's chosen process; this hub stores no progress.

Core assignment readiness

  • Grammar matrix: counts, terminals, names, integers, unknown commands, link ambiguity and duplicates.
  • Legal movement: identities, adjacency, once-per-ant, shared tunnel use, batch occupancy, completion and end absorption.
  • Exactness: greedy trap, full reduction proof, minimum-deadline proof and independent tiny-state evidence. Do not accept a route-count or shortest-path argument as a substitute.
  • Operational contract: deterministic bytes, stream/exit mapping, no premature echo, checked limits and no false optimum on refusal.
  • Compatibility: official valid/invalid examples, recorded timing cases and a source-revision note.
  • Code review: standard library, clear packages, deliberate errors, gofmt and meaningful tests/fuzzing. No core TODO stub remains.

Evidence review rubric

Review categories; all required categories must be demonstrated
CategoryEvidence to requestInsufficient evidence
Input correctnessTransition table and hostile fixturesOne accepted colony
Movement correctnessIndependent replay and targeted mutationsVisual inspection alone
Minimum turnsProof, T-1 witness and tiny oracle agreementA plausible greedy schedule
Resource behaviorPreflight/fault tests and measured audit timingComplexity notation without measurements
Bonus renderingDecode-back metadata, keyframe checks and viewed motionOne static screenshot

Planning and support

Core base estimate is 182 hours; with 25–50% review allowance, 228–273. Optional continuation adds 42 base hours. Reserve review sessions after P03, P06, P10, P12 and L01. The optimization block needs explicit hand traces and proof discussion, especially for learners who have never seen flow. Pairing can support reasoning, but each learner should explain the invariants and repair a failed test.

What this delivery verifies

See the validation record for publication links, starter compilation, curriculum structure, algorithm-model evidence and browser review. These are checks of the delivered learning material. They do not certify a completed student solver, cohort outcomes, external audit acceptance or deployment.

Title: Sources and academy adaptations
Body:
Sources and academy adaptations

Academy edition reviewed on 28 October 2026. Primary assignment source: 01-edu/public · lem-in. The inspected repository head was 13cd08c1d25db64e79535a51348c332f7dc83b9f. Source snapshots are preserved separately and are not rewritten as academy instructions.

Original material

  • Original subject snapshot · Pinned upstream subject.
  • Original audit snapshot · Pinned upstream audit.
  • Original examples snapshot · Pinned upstream examples.
  • Original good-practices snapshot · Pinned upstream good practices.

Local snapshots contain source content returned by the connected GitHub reader; the source manifest records local SHA-256 hashes and checked revision. They preserve the source's original examples and wording, including ambiguities and typos.

Interpretations verified against examples

  • The subject requires a file argument; an audit question calls it standard input. The curriculum follows the file-based executable usage and reserves stdin for the visualizer.
  • Unknown commands are ignored according to the subject. The audit's “only commands” language is interpreted as only start/end having semantic effects, rather than rejection of unknown directives.
  • Usage Example 2 demonstrates entering a room vacated during the same turn. The academy publishes batch departure/arrival semantics explicitly.
  • Each tunnel's once-per-turn rule applies even when both endpoints are unlimited-capacity terminals.
  • The subject's self-link error discussion and badexample01 support self-link rejection. Ordinary multiroom cycles are valid graph structures; safe traversal handles them.
  • Displayed audit schedules include formatting typos and need not be a unique optimum. Use source example data, legal-movement checks and exactness evidence; do not copy a displayed schedule as the complete test oracle.

Academy policies

The original source does not fully define whitespace, name-delimiter ambiguity, numeric spelling, echo byte normalization, streams/exits, tie-breaking or size limits. The exact contract marks those choices and provides tests. Local auditors may choose differently. The time-expanded flow algorithm is an academy teaching choice derived from the source capacity semantics, not an upstream mandated algorithm.

Algorithm and Go references

Go API behavior was checked against official module tutorials, Effective Go and standard package references linked in each guide. Graph/flow concepts use Princeton's graph material, maximum flow material, its study guide and MIT's integral-flow notes. Their non-Go examples are conceptual reading; every student implementation, scaffold and executable example here is Go.

Format and design provenance

The installed book-project-guide skill supplies the complete hands-on chapter pattern, TODO scaffolding and discussion counts. The user's requested forum dark styling overrides its default zero-CSS rule. The existing forum directory was used read-only: its shared dark stylesheet was copied into this new hub and adapted with a separate academy stylesheet. Its language selector and project count were not inherited. No existing Learning Hub files were edited.

Publication and external assumptions

The output is a static site. Publication instructions use a locally built public directory and a Vercel static configuration; Vercel's remote build image need not provide Go. No deployment was performed. External reading URLs, institutional audit interpretation, all shell/viewer combinations, cohort timing and performance of unfinished student implementations remain external or future verification tasks. The hub's own evidence report distinguishes these from checks actually run.

Title: Build and publication
Body:
Reproducible build and publication

The authoring source, Go builder, unfinished starter modules and generated public directory belong to this standalone hub. Students need Go for their exercises; publication needs no package-manager installation.

Build locally

go run ./cmd/hub build
go run ./cmd/hub check -scaffolds
go test ./...
go vet ./...
go run ./cmd/hub serve

Run at the academy root. The preview serves http://127.0.0.1:8086. The build reads curriculum/projects, pages and coverage data, writes every complete guide in order, formats Go starters, creates deterministic ZIP downloads and copies static assets/sources/evidence into public. The check command validates generated HTML structure, local links/anchors, preparation order, guide counts, coverage IDs and optional nested starter module compilation/vet.

Reproducibility and editing

Edit curriculum data or the shared assets, then rebuild. Do not edit generated public pages or the supplied starter copies after beginning student work. ZIP timestamps and ordering are fixed. The generated site has no runtime API, browser script or external font dependency. Evidence files record the particular validation run and may change when checks are rerun.

Vercel-ready static output

The included vercel.json selects no framework and publishes public. Its build command checks that the already-generated index, roadmap and validation page exist. This deliberately avoids assuming Go is installed on Vercel's remote build image. Before any future requested deployment, rebuild/check locally and include the resulting public directory with the project. The root's authoring source can remain private if publishing public alone.

Vercel output-directory documentation and build-image documentation were consulted. The local build and configuration are verified; remote deployment and project settings are not, because this hub has not been deployed.

Distribution

Serve public with any static server or open index.html locally for offline browsing. External reading links still need a network connection. If moving the site, retain all relative guide/download/assets paths. A ZIP of the complete academy workspace is supplied separately for review and further editing.

Title: Validation record
Body:
Validation record

Delivery checked on 29 October 2026. This record validates the curriculum, publication output, unfinished scaffolds and the teaching model. It does not certify a completed student solver or automatically assess learner progress.

Publication and scaffold checks

  • 255 generated HTML pages across 16 full guides, including 228 guide chapters plus guide indexes and academy pages.
  • Generated structure, local navigation/anchors/download paths, preparation dependency order and all 36 coverage rows checked with the Go hub checker.
  • Every generated route checked through Go's static HTTP handler without a listening socket.
  • All 16 nested starter modules compile with go test and pass go vet using the local Go toolchain. Their acceptance tests are explicitly skipped and core algorithms remain TODOs.
  • The hub build/check tooling has separate tests for malformed markup, duplicate anchors and escaped navigation data.

Detailed structural/scaffold results · Pinned source hashes.

Independent algorithm-model experiment

A scratch experiment compared an exhaustive occupancy-multiset BFS with the time-expanded integer-flow feasibility model on all 3294 labelled graph/ant cases for V=2..5, terminals 0 and V-1, n=1..3. There were no mismatches and no budget skips. A separately targeted eight-room greedy trap with four ants also agreed at five turns. The experiment explored 25507 oracle states in total.

Model experiment results, methods and scratch-source hash. This tiny mathematical evidence complements the written correctness arguments. It is not a file parser, complete solver, performance audit or ready-made student solution.

Viewed layout and navigation

The static pages were rendered in Chromium at 1440×900 and 390×844, with dark color scheme and reduced motion. Every route was captured at both widths; overflow, main/heading presence and page loads were checked. Representative overview, guide, library and coverage screenshots plus route contact sheets were visually inspected. Home-to-roadmap, roadmap-to-guide, chapter-next/index navigation and starter download interactions were exercised at both sizes.

Browser review and per-route measurements. Download navigation cancellation is expected when the browser hands a ZIP to its download manager; the actual download filename is checked separately.

Reproduce the local publication checks

go run ./cmd/hub build
go run ./cmd/hub check -scaffolds
go test ./...
go vet ./...

Limits and future gates

  • Browser loopback networking was unavailable in the execution environment; visual checks used local file URLs, and the static HTTP handler was tested separately.
  • Chromium mobile emulation is not a physical device, WebKit or screen-reader audit. Other browser/shell/viewer combinations remain unverified.
  • Student acceptance tests, source audit solver performance, bonus rendering by student code and cohort estimates remain future instructional gates.
  • Primary references were researched and pinned source content compared; future availability of every external URL is not guaranteed.
  • Vercel configuration and real public output are included. No remote build, push, publication or deployment was performed.
